record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: If X has the γ-property S1(Ω, Γ) and D is a set of reals of size less than p, must X ∪ D still satisfy S1(Ω, Γ)? Under Martin’s Axiom, must this remain true when |D| = ℵ1?

evidence.quote: Assume that X satisfies S1(Ω, Γ) and |D| < p. Does X ∪ D satisfy S1(Ω, Γ)? Is it true under Martin’s Axiom when |D| = ℵ1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a set of real numbers. For a topological space (or subspace of the reals) Y, denote by Ω(Y) the family of open ω-covers of Y, i.e. collections U of open sets such that Y itself is not in U and every finite subset of Y is contained in some member of U. Denote by Γ(Y) the family of open γ-covers of Y, i.e. infinite open covers U of Y such that every point of Y belongs to all but finitely many members of U.

A space Y satisfies the selection principle S1(Ω, Γ) (the γ-property) if for every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ω} with each U_n ∈ Ω(Y) there exist U_n ∈ U_n such that {U_n : n ∈ ω} ∈ Γ(Y).

Let p denote the pseudo-intersection number: the least cardinality of a family F of infinite subsets of ω that is closed under finite intersections (has the strong finite intersection property) but admits no infinite A ⊆ ω with A ⊆* F for every F ∈ F.

Questions.
(1) Suppose X ⊆ ℝ satisfies S1(Ω, Γ) and D ⊆ ℝ has |D| < p. Must X ∪ D satisfy S1(Ω, Γ)?
(2) Assume Martin's Axiom. If X ⊆ ℝ satisfies S1(Ω, Γ) and D ⊆ ℝ has |D| = ℵ_1, must X ∪ D satisfy S1(Ω, Γ)?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not return definitive evidence resolving these specific questions about whether the γ-property S1(Ω, Γ) is preserved when adjoining a set of reals of cardinality less than p (or of size ℵ_1 under MA). Related results on γ-sets and unions exist, but no explicit solution to these particular preservation questions was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses γ-sets, selection principles, and behavior under Martin's Axiom; under MA there is a γ-set of size continuum.

status_evidence.snippet: Under MA, unions of fewer than continuum many measure-zero (resp. meager) sets remain such; analogous preservation results for selection principles are not stated.
status_evidence.claim: General MA preservation context, but not specific to S1(Ω, Γ) unions.
